To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the colour-magnitude relations of elliptical galaxies can be understood as the consequence of an age spread, and that this age spread is the consequence of an efficiency of star formation which increases with the galaxy mass.

the colour-magnitude sequence in early-type galaxies is a consequence of the combination of two trends with galaxy mass, one in age (decreasing with mass) and one in star formation efficiency (increasing with mass), and that the trend with mass in age can be explained in terms of the infall time.
the colour-magnitude sequence of elliptical galaxies requires a spread in age and metallicity.

elliptical galaxies are the result of the merger of gas-rich galaxies.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the colour-magnitude sequence in elliptical galaxies is not an age sequence, and that the age-metallicity relation is not a simple one, with the age of the stellar population increasing with mass.
the observed [Mg/ Fe] vs. mass trend can be understood in terms of infall and outflows, with an age spread which is consistent with the observed colour-magnitude relation.

the observed [Mg/ Fe] trend in early-type galaxies can only be understood if we assume that the duration of star-formation is a strong function of mass, and that the star formation efficiency is a weak function of mass.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the observed [Mg/ Fe] and colour-magnitude relation in elliptical galaxies can be explained in a self-consistent scenario of star formation and metal enrichment, which does not rely on any fine tuning of parameters.
the observed correlation between [MFe] and mass can only be reproduced by a scenario in which the star formation is prolonged and efficient, with a mass-dependent efficiency, in massive galaxies.
the colour-magnitude and age-metallicity relations in elliptical galaxies are consistent with the idea that massive ellipticals form from a gas-rich progenitor with a long-lived star formation phase.
